by_judge.judge: C M POONACHA WILL SIT IN COURT HALL NO.6 AT DHARWAD
P SREE SUDHA IS NOT HOLDING SITTING ON 14.08.2026

narrative:
On August 14, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,580 matters across 65 benches and heard 950 cases, resulting in an overall hearing rate of 36.8%. The day's workload reflected an expanded docket relative to prior sessions, such as July 31 (2,307 scheduled, 38.1% heard) and July 17 (2,108 scheduled, 49.2% heard). Despite the higher listing volume, total clearances remained comparable to earlier sittings, sustaining a moderate hearing rate below 40%.

The procedural workload was led by Orders, which accounted for 978 listings with 389 heard (39.8%). Admission stages demonstrated stronger conversion, completing 173 of 365 scheduled hearings (47.4%). In contrast, Final Hearings experienced a bottleneck, converting only 100 of 564 scheduled matters (17.7%), down from 25.5% on July 31 and 35.0% on July 17. By case category, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest block with 1,306 listings and a 29.7% hearing rate (388 heard). Appellate and criminal rosters maintained higher clearance, with Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) reaching 50.1% (172 of 343 heard) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieving 46.3% (124 of 268 heard).

Bench-level progress showed considerable variation across halls. High-throughput benches included Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 20, who heard 64 of 76 cases (84.2%) on his primary list, and Justice M. Nagaprasanna in Hall 14, who heard 69 of 130 matters (53.1%). Conversely, heavy roster sizes constrained progress in certain courts; Justice B. M. Shyam Prasad heard 1 of 260 scheduled cases on a primary list in Hall 6, while Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar heard 7 of 82 scheduled cases (8.5%) in Hall 22.
